beliefs.practice: Read the DOCUMENTDB_URI from an environment variable (not checked into source) and create a single shared MongoClient at app startup; reuse that client across modules instead of opening a new connection per request.

Tune MongoClient pool settings in the connection string (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) and enable unified topology; set reasonable serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS so the app detects and recovers from unreachable cluster quickly.
Always require TLS/SSL (e.g., tls=true/ssl=true in the connection string) and do not disable certificate validation when connecting to the DocumentDB cluster.

Do not store database credentials or connection strings in the repository; load secrets from environment variables or a secrets store (Azure Key Vault) and grant the app least-privilege access to them.
Use a dedicated, least-privilege database user for the application (not the cluster admin), with only the minimum roles/privileges needed to read/write the application collections.
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors and rate-limited responses (handle HTTP 429/Retry-After from Cosmos), and enable retryableWrites where appropriate.

Perform slot booking/rescheduling with an atomic conditional update (e.g., updateOne({_id:slotId, status:'available'}, {$set:{status:'booked', appointmentId:...}})) and check modifiedCount to detect conflicts instead of separate read-then-write.

For multi-document invariants (e.g., create appointment document AND mark slot booked), use a multi-document transaction when supported by the MongoDB API version in the cluster; otherwise implement a safe compensating pattern and detect partial failures.
Create a compound index supporting the most common availability queries, for example {providerId:1, startTime:1, status:1}, and ensure index creation is idempotent in the seed script.

Use unique indexes for fields that must be unique (e.g., appointment._id or a unique appointmentReference) and enforce uniqueness at the DB level where possible; do not rely solely on application checks to prevent duplicates.

If storing embeddings for vector search, store them as a consistent-dimension numeric array (e.g., embedding: [float,...]) and create a vector index configured with the correct dimension and metric (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) supported by the cluster.

Provision throughput sensibly: use autoscale or an appropriately sized RU/s for the database/collection; for development use lower single-collection throughput and for production scale based on load and RU cost of booking flows.
Monitor RU consumption and avoid operations that require large RU spikes (large scans, unindexed sorts); respond to 429 by backing off and throttling client request rate.

Avoid unbounded collection scans: always filter on indexed fields and use projection to only return required fields (e.g., when listing availability return providerId, startTime, duration, status only).
Make the seed script idempotent: create collections and indexes only if they don't exist, and use upsert operations or checks so running seed multiple times does not create duplicates.
Use TTL indexes for ephemeral records (e.g., temporary holds or short-lived conversation state) by adding an ISODate field (expireAt) and a TTL index so the DB automatically expires stale data.

When updating documents in place prefer findOneAndUpdate with an atomic modifier and an appropriate returnDocument option (return the new state) to reduce round-trips and ensure you get the final state to update memory/agent context.
Avoid storing or logging sensitive patient information in plaintext in logs; redact or omit PII from logs and secure exported DB backups.

For conversation memory and agent state, persist only necessary identifiers (conversationId, lastAppointmentId) in the DB and keep full conversational context ephemeral in the agent memory; encrypt sensitive persisted state at rest if required.
Create text indexes for free-text search fields (e.g., provider name, specialty) if the app needs text search, and restrict text indexes to the fields actually needed to limit index size and RU cost.

Design documents for the access patterns: keep a single slot per document (slot document) and a separate appointments collection that references slotId, to allow targeted atomic updates on slots without large document rewrites.
Protect the Cosmos account with network restrictions (IP firewall rules or VNet/private endpoint) so only allowed application hosts can reach the DocumentDB endpoint.

When performing reschedule logic that changes slot times, check for overlapping slots for the same provider using an indexed query and enforce application-level checks to prevent overlapping bookings (DB-level partial unique constraints on time ranges are not broadly supported).
Instrument and trace booking/rescheduling flows (record latency, RU cost, success/failure) so you can detect hotspots and tune indexes or RU provisioning accordingly.

Index the fields used for sorting (e.g., startTime) so that queries that sort by startTime can use an index rather than a blocking sort; prefer covered queries (projection includes only indexed fields) where possible to reduce RU.
